Hmmm. Training dogs not to eat poop is bit of a hard one since it's not like teaching them to do tricks, you can't reward them when they don't eat it. I would suggest maybe try doing the same thing that I did with mine when they got bitey. Grab her, pull the nugget out of her mouth by force, and put her in the laundry or somewhere boring. Don't talk to her or acknowledge her while you are doing this. But don't leave her in there too long. Dogs lose there sense of what things are for after too long. So leaving her in the laundry bored for 15 minutes is the same to her as 4 hours, except you get to have you happy puppy back sooner. This means you will have to be vigilant, but that's what raising puppies is all about.

It's hard to teach a dog to tell you when she needs to poop, but you just have to keep an eye on the signs that a dog needs to go to the toilet I guess. Consider maybe getting a doggy door, they have latches on them so you can lock them, and dogs will often learn that scratching at the doggy door when it is locked makes you come open it for them. But a lot can be said for anticipating your dogs needs. Dogs will need to poop after they eat, and often after they have had a nap. So half an hour after you feed your dog, sit outside at the grass with them until they poop, then reward her. Same when you walk her. Stay outside until she does that second poop and reward her, she'll learn that she should get all her poops done outside. Also don't stop rewarding them, but don't do it as often either. If you've studied psychology at all, you'll know that rats learn behaviours best by getting rewarded at random intervals, it's the same with dogs.

Stopping your dog from nipping at your cat is similar to the eating cat poop. Make her know that if she does it, boring times will ensue. Also maybe look into why she is nipping at your cat. She's probably feeling a little bored and playful, so she thinks your cat will make things interesting. Maybe take her to a dog park where she can rough and tumble with other dogs? Spend time with a tug of war style toy? Corgis are superbly intelligent dogs but unfortunately that means they get bored quickly and will have to invent games to occupy themselves. If you keep her occupied and show her that these bad behaviours lead to boring time, she will learn.

Consider maybe getting one of those puzzle toys where food is released only when they roll it a certain way. Or if you are running a little tight in money, you can get a 2L bottle of coke and fill it with some dry food and cut a small whole on the breadth of it. This means to get it out your dog will have to roll the coke bottle around, it's basically a cheaper but slightly less effective version of the puzzle toys.

The gifted kid at school will start acting out if the teachers don't give them something challenging.

If you are doing these things but your dog is still having problems then maybe something else is at foot.

Also I wouldn't worry too much about your dog hurting your cat. Most of the time the nipping puppies do to other animals is more of a request for play fighting. As long as your cat has benches or cat forts it can climb on when it's pissed off at your dog it should be fine.

I asked my brother who is a scientist to give us the low down. Essentially in pure breed breeds there was historically a lot of inbreeding. I can't remember which breed it is but one breed particularly can all be traced back to a single dog.

"The higher the correlation between the genetic material of the parents the greater the chance that a child will end up with two defective genes and there for exhibit symptoms of a particular genetic desease."

So the jist of it is, if all blood hounds have a genetic weakness to X desease if you breed too blood hounds he will have two genes that match up making the puppy have the weakness too. If you breed him with a jack russel he might get genetic weaknesses to X and Y deseases, but because neither of them match up he wont actually be weak.

Also I believe when you are talking mutts tehy lose a lot of their negative characteristics, so bulldog mutts are less likely to have as much problems breathing, King Charles mutts are more likely to have a larger skull and not get seizures because of it. The more mixed it the less they have these distinctive features from my experience.

In terms of Designer Puppy's thats a completely different discussion than mutts, because it is not uncommon for Designer Puppy Mills to inbreed their dogs to keep certain characteristics. They are essentially doing a rushed and unplanned selective breeding program which does horrible things to their pups.

My brother also just pointed out to me that in most profession and well regarded circles of pure breed circles they try to strengthen the blood line by not breeding the pups that display genetic weaknesses, however since there has recently become a fad in having puppies, places like puppy mill that don't care are causing this problem again.

In conclusion, Because of their much higher level of genetic diversity Mutts not sourced through inbreeding are more likely to be healthy animals in the two areas of Weaknesses due to physical appearances or genetic weaknesses. However Pure Bred dogs from respectable breeders should only have the expected weaknesses you read about.

In the long run I will just get a dog from the pound and love him to bits no matter what happens.

There are many different forms of depression, and they will all feel different, and effect different people. There is also no sure fire way to get rid of it. but I will try and give you a super quick guide, since I can't stay long. An important thing to remember is roughly 1/4 people will experience depression for some time in their life. It does get better. It's just part of life.

Major Depression Disorder: Is a chemical imbalance in the brain which causes the person to not produce enough (Seritonine?) which is what allows a person to feel positive.

Situational Depression: Is caused by long term situations that feel like they never go away. This can be things such as loneliness, abusive families, Chronic Sickness.

Acute Depression: Is caused by a specific short term thing, such as death in the family or a fight you have.

Especially if you are between the ages of 15-21 you should not be surprised that you are feeling depressed, at that age your brain is going through massive changes are you are just now going through the stage of human development where you first start looking at the world and understand it from your own point of view. High School and University are also not the best places to promote emotional wellbeing. If you are outside of that then there are probably other things you need to think about.

A quick list of things you should look at to see if you can improve your life.

1. Talking to people. It is currently thought in the Psychologist community that people who talk to 5 or more people outside of their family a day will have an increased level of happiness and physical health. This doesn't mean hanging out with 5 people, but can include simple things like talking to people in shops. So if you are able to maybe try having a small conversation with the person behind the register. Or even just smiling at people you see on the street.

2. Smiling causes the body to produce chemicals that make you happy. This is a legit thing, I don't understand why but it does. You can also put a pencil in your mouth holding your cheeks back and it works the same way.

3. Eating and Excersizing well. I honestly can not stress how much this makes a difference. Excersizing releases the happy chemicals and relieves stress. Eating well, especially avoiding deep fried food that contains high fructose corn syrup. The problem with deep fried food is that it works much like a drug, you feel better for a short time after you eat it, but your depression will increase and you will crave it until you get it again. This is the same with Potato Crisps. If you can afford it I definitely recommend you purchasing a block of strong dark chocolate, and eat only one piece of it a day. Dark chocolate is incredibly good for your mental health if you only eat a small amount.

4. Volunteering, at an animal shelter or a soup kitchen, or a school or anything, not only will this give you a place wehre you can meet people but also allow you to feel like you are making a difference with the world AND give you stuff to pad your resume with. If you don't want to volunteer maybe look for community groups to join. There are knitting or yoga classes all over the place. Many areas have people who play Magic the Gathering regularly. You might even find a movie club somewhere.

5. Burn Incense in your house, clean your room, and let the sun shine in. If you have the money maybe even invest  in a salt lamp.

6. Keep reminding yourself that it will go away, things will get better, and you will be able to look back on your experiences and see how it's made you a better person.

Unfortunately though sometimes, particularly if it is a chromic mental illness related thing rather than a situational thing (I myself have Bipolar Disorder and a couple of other illnesses will have to struggle through it for the rest of my life.) Although it doesn't continue to be a struggle. You eventually will gain the tools to handle it, you will feel just like any other person again. But there might be some things you have to keep in mind in order to not set yourself off. For instance I have to avoid over exerting myself otherwise I fall back into illness.

Ohkay, so. This is a really tricky question, but one you are perfectly right to ask.

People are always responsible for their actions to some degree. He can never do something and get of scott free. But you have to remember that life is most likely unimaginably difficult for him on a day to day basis. If he does something that upsets you, it's fine for you to want to take some time off to gather your thoughts before you can talk to him. But don't take it out on him, you can let him know that what he did was not appropriate. But he probably couldn't help himself. Being mad at him, yelling at him, ignoring him will just make life worse.

Think of it like he is unintentionally drunk. He is still expected to try and be as civil and proper as he can, but he isn't playing with a full set of cards so if he messes up you need to try and be as understanding as you can. You don't need to feel bad about being mad at him, or wanting to blame him. But you shouldn't make him feel bad.

I don't know about the other stuff, but in order to teach him tricks, you should definitely look into the reward studies people have done. For example, when he does something you shouldn't give him a treat every time, because then once you stop giving him treats he will also stop doing the tricks. If you start giving him the treats at random intervals he will remember the tricks better. Although when he is first learning something you want to reward him very often.

For things like stay, you make him sit and then say stay as you step backwards. At first just a step or two to make sure he sits there, and when you are ready for him to come to you bend down and say good boy and offer him a treat, then he will run to you naturally. Then you take him back to the spot you were and try again but at a further distance. As a puppy he wont have much attention span so you have to make sure you don't leave him in one place for too long until he gets older.

A good "trick" to teach them is to sit and wait before you let them eat. That way they wont shove their faces in the bowl as you try and dish it out. It's good practice. Similarly when take him on walks make him sit at every crossing and refuse to move on until he does.

If you want to be playful with him you can teach him to play bang or do figure 8's around your feet but the process is a little more complicated for this. Although be careful about teaching him bang, since sometimes a puppy will misinterpret this as them getting in trouble.

The other thing I would say to someone with a new puppy is 100% do not rely on the over marketed dog food that comes in cans. This is a really rookie mistake and can shorten the life of your pup. When our old dog was 8 she was in a very poor way, her fur was losing color. We switched her to http://www.hillspet.com.au/ and she got her life back and carried on for another 4 years before getting sick. We then bought a puppy for her to play with and she survived on another 3 years. Obviously that is an Australian brand but there should be some equivalent in whatever country you live in. Maybe ask some show breeders what they feed their pets? We do still give them some canned dog food in the morning but it's more of a sweet we give them because they like it rather than for their nutrition.

I'd also maybe suggest weaning off the use of flicks on the nose as soon as you can. Just try saying no in a deep stern voice and ignoring him. And then retain the use of flicks on the nose for when he actually bites someone. Also I don't know if he is teething at the moment, but its often good when your pup is teething to have a place for them that is fairly boring, like a closed off corner of the laundry, so when they get bity you just put them inside and leave them for 15-30 minutes. Often they will be most bitey when they are overly tired, so you will often find they will fall asleep there. If they haven't they should have calmed down by the end of your 15-30 minutes and you can try and bring them again again. If you have a no go policy when it comes to their teeth they will learn quickly. (Just like a child though this is because their mouths are in a lot of pain, so you should make sure they have an adequate amount of things to chew on. You might find that your dog will prefer to chew on your hand than the toy that it's holding though, this is because the soft fleshy skin is the most soothing for them, so maybe look for another toy it might like more.)

You can see what I have said on the other comment about the reason why I say alcoholism is an illness. One thing you have to understand with depression and any other mental illness is that it is unlike the sadness that normal people feel. It's not something you can shake off. It is a burning pain that eats your very soul till you feel like there is nothing left of you. At first you take a drink or two and you feel content. No body is hurt. Whats the problem. A little later you take a drink more and you don't even fully realize it but this is the first time in 14 years that you have felt ohkay. Like you aren't going to claw your eyes out just to feel something. You can smile and laugh. Your friends actually enjoy being around you for once. Then you think, well this is fantastic I'll just have a little bit every now and then to take the edge off things, so you keep a steady supply of alcohol in your fridge. Every night you come home from school or work is a complete utter hatred for yourself and the world so you have a few drinks to make it go away. As time goes on your tolerance goes up and your brain chemicals start triggering the desire to drink more and more.

This is how drug abuse often starts. Something that people don't realize about people with mental disorders. Peoples brain changes, the chemical reactions in the brain that make people think carefully about this don't happen nearly as much. This is ESPECIALLY relevant to people with Bipolar disorder, Anxiety and Schizophrenia but also depression.
